literature_name: Ruminococcoides intestinale (most genomes carry the NCBI name Ruminococcus bromii)
name_note: Ruminococcoides intestinale is a recently named species; most genomes GTDB places here carry the NCBI name Ruminococcus bromii, so work on that species describes close relatives.

sentences.text: Ruminococcoides intestinale was named from a public collection of cultured human gut strains as a previously unknown dominant species, reported there as associated with health.
Ruminococcus bromii, the name carried by most genomes placed here, is a dominant gut member that releases energy from dietary starches escaping host digestion.
Its amylase activity is expressed constitutively and its enzymes are organised into an extracellular complex, the amylosome, built on dockerin-bearing proteins.
Amylosome components are conserved between human colonic strains from three continents and a strain from cattle rumen, reflecting extreme specialisation on starch.
In 46 healthy adults, bands attributed to uncultivated bacteria closely related to this species rose on diets high in resistant starch.
